candidate.description_text:
Desired outcome: SMAR3TS project partner - TalTech is looking for innovative approaches to apply Circular Economy Principles to the current challenges in Housing/Construction Development. The construction sector has traditionally followed a linear path: build, use, demolish, discard. This approach is no longer seen as sustainable in Estonia. Globally the built environment is responsible for about 40% of CO₂ emissions, nearly 1/3 of all waste and 1/2 of Europe’s resource use. To correspond to climate targets and create sustainable urban futures, cities must move towards circular construction by reusing what already exists instead of discarding it. TalTech Department of Business Administration is currently involved in several sustainability-related projects, most relevant for current I3X proposal: Reusing Old Buildings for Circular Construction. R&I stages: ☐ Idea / Conceptualization ☐ Pilot / Proof of Concept ☐ Early Implementation The Innovate3X (I3X) challenge (described here as a call to innovate solutions for resilience, restoration, and regeneration) invites research and innovation talent within the SMAR3TS project to contribute to the development of innovations for circular economy in housing/construction through secondments at Taltech in Tallinn, Estonia. To address this I3X challenge future secondees could work on identifying solutions to Market & Adoption-related challenges, conduct Sustainability & Assessment, provide a better understanding of Regulation & Policy, as well as Societal & Cultural trends.

Express your interest in SMAR3TS secondment - Your opportunity at Taltech (Tallinn, Estonia) This I3X challenge is initiated by Taltech within the SMAR3TS project and requires a secondment with a minimum duration of 30 days (to take place starting from Dec 2025). Fully funded by the European Commission, the four-year SMAR3TS project started in October 2025 and unites 35 partners worldwide to accelerate resilient, restorative and regenerative transitions through research and innovation mobility. For more info: please see details in the attachments. Please note : the secondments are open only to SMAR3TS Consortium Partners. Necessary skills and capabilities across disciplines - For a problem related to the buildings which contain durable and valuable components with high reuse potential, there is currently no standardized way to identify, recover and reallocate these materials - as a solution – there is a need for a standardized pre-demolition audit methodology to identify materials with reuse potential . - One of the solutions would a registry/Marketplace in the format of a digital platform, skills are needed to create this tool/environment, accessible for developers. - Learning about the best practices in other European countries (including the barriers and enablers in this process) will be most valuable to solve the problems related to the reuse of building materials. Examples of challenges that need to be addressed - Market & Adoption-related challenges : S calability of reuse of construction materials extracted from old buildings is applicable only in the case where newer buildings need similar unified materials and their location is nearby demolition site, otherwise the costs will be higher than using materials based on virgin components. - Sustainability & Assessment of innovative business models for new technologies in construction-related sectors. - Regulation & Policy : Construction developers meet challenges when considering materials from demolished or unused buildings, as there is a lack of standardized certificates concerning these materials that could be included in new buildings. The reliability, durability and other aspects are in question. Finding innovative solutions for evaluating each old building separately for each type of reusable material is time and resource consuming (expensive). - Societal & Cultural : There are communities that are ready to consume (=live) in the buildings where reusable materials are in use, but they still form a minority. The issues of social acceptance need constant attention and context-specific solutions. I3X at Taltech – About the initiator 1. Background info TalTech is internationally recognized research-based university; leading provider of engineering and economic education in Estonia. Website: www.taltech.ee 2. Research Group/Company Department The Unit deals with the tasks and processes aiming at preparing and supporting the implementation of growth opportunities and innovations in companies, focusing on preparing, planning, implementing and evaluating a continuous stream of potential innovations; investigation of potential growth and innovation opportunities within and between organizations by using interdisciplinary approaches from business, sustainability management (e.g. circular economy) and environmental economics, operations and innovation management, engineering, IT, design and social sciences; in the context of the European agenda for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. Link to the website : https://taltech.ee/en/department-business-administration Contact : Tarmo Tuisk, Project Specialist , tarmo.tuisk@taltech.ee See attachment: Expertise and available technologies at Taltech within SMAR3TS project and examples of strategically relevant I3X Initiatives. Alignment to Work-Packages (Nutrition, Mobility, Energy, Housing) SMAR3TS domains that are relevant to the work of TalTech organization/research and innovation team: Sustainable Value Chain Management Unit at TalTech Department of Business Administration deals with the tasks and processes aiming at preparing and supporting the implementation of growth opportunities and innovations in companies, focusing on preparing, planning, implementing and evaluating a continuous stream of potential innovations; investigation of potential growth and innovation opportunities within and between organizations by using interdisciplinary approaches from business, sustainability management (e.g. circular economy) and environmental economics, operations and innovation management, engineering, IT, design and social sciences. Within this umbrella, there is ongoing research on circular economy business models that is directly related to construction and adjacent sectors such as wood or metal industry, or reuse of old buildings as building material. Alignment to Resilience, Restoration, Regeneration (R3) Through the circular economy framework, Units’ research is aligned with all three R3 elements: resilience, restoration and regeneration. Circular business models enhance the adaptive capacity of local economies by reducing dependence on global supply chains and by stabilising resource flows. Approaches such as material recirculation or modular construction support more efficient primary use and systematic reuse of locally sourced building materials. This, in turn, strengthens the resilience of local firms and communities by fostering resource security, promoting local value creation, and reducing exposure to external shocks as well as contributing to restoration by lowering the ecological footprint of construction activities, mitigating waste generation, and enabling the reintegration of secondary materials into production processes. Note: The expression of interest for the secondment at TalTech must be submitted via the platform. Submissions will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and you will be contacted as soon as possible. For any questions, please contact: info@smar3ts.eu

candidate.description_text: Desired outcome: SMAR3TS project partner - PARE is looking for innovative solutions to improve the Resilience of Multifunctional Neighborhoods within the 15-minutes City Concept: Workplaces Perspective. PARE (Estonian HR Association) is at concept stage for a program on workplace-neighborhoods—how the immediate public realm around worksites (5–15-minute catchments) relates to HR outcomes (well-being, engagement, absenteeism/presenteeism, retention). PARE does not have an internal R&D unit; our role is to convene employers, broker academic–city partnerships, and translate evidence into HR practice. In the current stage of ideation, the goal is to identify perspective partners to form a consortium (PARE + university methods lead + municipal/landlord partners). Potential areas of research, innovation, and engagement work that can be achieved within the secondment include the following: - Evidence & Theory: scoping review; theory of change (neighborhood → exposures/behaviors → HR outcomes). - Measurement Design: WNQI v0.1 (objective GIS/remote-sensing candidates; short perception scales; HR-relevant outcomes); data protection plan. - Stakeholder engagement: interviews/workshops with employers, city units, and landlords; site selection and MoUs. - Pilot readiness: pre-analysis plans (DiD/event-study templates), instrument list (steps/usage, short affect scales), feasibility testing of data flows.
candidate.title: Improving Resilience of Multifunctional Neighborhoods within 15-minutes City Concept: Workplaces Perspective (PARE, Estonia)

candidate.description_text:
Desired outcome: SMAR3TS project partner IfM Engage is looking for innovative approaches to support the development and adoption of sustainable and regenerative food packaging solutions, with a focus on new materials and system-level integration. Food packaging is essential for food safety, quality and shelf- life, yet it is also a major contributor to plastic pollution, resource depletion and waste generation. While innovation in bio-based, biodegradable and recyclable materials is advancing rapidly, many solutions remain difficult to scale due to performance limitations, cost barriers, regulatory complexity and poor integration with food systems. Within the SMAR3TS project, this I3X focuses on moving beyond isolated material substitution and supporting regenerative packaging approaches that reduce environmental impact, minimise food waste and align with circular economy and sustainability objectives across food systems.

Initiator: IfM Engage (Institute for Manufacturing, University of Cambridge), United Kingdom ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ IfM Engage is a knowledge transfer organization embedded in the Institute for Manufacturing (IfM) (a division of the Engineering Department at the University of Cambridge ). ​ IfM Engage focuses on facilitating knowledge translation from the research happening at IfM and the wider university to practice, supporting industry and government through the deployment of consulting, education and communication activities. ​ The group prepares and supports the implementation of innovation and transformation initiatives by connecting academic research with real-world decision-making and delivery. In general the methods deployed are versatile and can be adapted to various contexts/sectors. IfM Engage have much experience to deploy our approaches in all the 4 sectors (Nutrition, Mobility, Energy and Housing). ​ IfM Engage’s work draws on interdisciplinary approaches and has run activities in a variety of sectors including Food, Energy, Mobility and Construction. Across the sectors, the focus is on innovation and operations management, sustainability and resilience management, policy studies, systems engineering and digitalization and social sciences, in the context of European and global agendas for sustainable, resilient and inclusive growth. Case studies which describe IfM Engage capabilities include: https://engage.ifm.eng.cam.ac.uk/e-wave-powering-the-future-of-electric-shipping/ https://www.ifm.eng.cam.ac.uk/insights/sustainability/ https://engage.ifm.eng.cam.ac.uk/project/eit-food-roadmapping-case-study/ https://engage.ifm.eng.cam.ac.uk/project/unlocking-the-potential-of-materials-for-quantum-technologies-in-the-uk/ https://engage.ifm.eng.cam.ac.uk/project/future-proofing-controlled-environment-agriculture-with-defra/ This I3X is Looking for Skills and Capabilities across Disciplines for: Food packaging and materials innovation Circular economy and life-cycle assessment Sustainability and systems thinking Innovation management and scaling Policy and regulatory analysis (food contact materials, waste) Stakeholder coordination across food and packaging value chains Important: ​ ​ SMAR3TS Secondments are open only to SMAR3TS Consortium Partners. ​ ​ Secondments aligned to any I3X can be undertaken at either the Initiating Parter premises and/or other SMAR3TS Consortium Partner premises. ​ ​ Regardless of where you are undertaking work on an I3X, you are obligated to ensure the aligned I3X Initiator Project Contact, Lead / Responsible aligned Work Package Leader, as well as the SMAR3TS Project Management Team are kept fully up-to-date with the progress of your contribution to your secondment aligned I3X - Refer to the detailed information ' About Secondments - What are Secondments '. Examples of Challenges that Need to be Addressed Fragmented packaging innovation landscape : New materials are being developed, but without coordinated evaluation across manufacturing, recycling, cost and regulation. Short-term vs long-term sustainability trade-offs: Companies must decide how to improve sustainability now while also preparing for future packaging systems and legislation. Infrastructure compatibility: Many new materials fail because they do not work with existing sorting, recycling or reuse systems. Regulatory and investment uncertainty: Rapidly evolving policy (e.g. plastics regulation, EPR, recycling targets) makes it difficult to make long-term packaging investments. Key research question : How should the food and drink industry and supply chain plan and coordinate to deliver more sustainable packaging – both quick wins in the short-term and taking advantage of the most advanced opportunities emerging from new materials, designs and manufacturing approaches? The secondments should contribute across various disciplines to help bring scientific developments into practice and support the future of packaging sustainability in the food industry. Initiator Institution (IfM Engage @ the University of Cambridge) Contact for this I3X Link to the website: https://engage.ifm.eng.cam.ac.uk Project Lead: Dr Michèle Routley, IfM Engage Industrial Associate, Institute for Manufacturing, mjr88@cam.ac.uk Dr David Lott, Chief Executive Officer, IfM Engage, Institute for Manufacturing, dl362@cam.ac.uk NOTE: Click here for instructions on how to plan for a secondment. Alignment to Work-Package/s SMAR3TS domains that are relevant to this I3X: ​ Lead Work Package, Nutrition – food systems, packaging, food quality and waste reduction In addition, IfM has much experience experience to deploy its approaches in all the 4 SMAR3TS Domains (Nutrition, Mobility, Energy and Housing). ​ Background: https://engage.ifm.eng.cam.ac.uk/project/the-problem-of-plastic-open-innovation-forum-tackles-sustainable-packaging/ https://engage.ifm.eng.cam.ac.uk/new-national-framework-for-materials-4-in-the-uk/ SMAR3TS Nutrition Work Package Lead Contact: Assoc. Prof. Letizia Mortara, University of Cambridge, IfM, lm367@cam.ac.uk Alignment to Resilience, Restoration, Regeneration (R3) Regenerative food packaging strengthens resilience by reducing dependency on fossil-based materials and improving food system robustness. It contributes to restoration by lowering environmental impacts from packaging waste, and supports regeneration by enabling circular and regenerative material systems. candidate.description_text:
Desired outcome: Nomad Foods seeks advanced in-line or on-line measurement solutions for breadcrumb-coated products (e.g., fish fingers) to enable real-time monitoring of critical quality attributes. Desired capabilities include: - Particle size distribution across individual products and product ranges - Surface area and topography of coated products - Breadcrumb particle porosity and internal structure - Predictive modelling of sensory-related texture attributes such as crispiness, oiliness, and hardness based on measurement data The objective is to improve process control and ensure consistent product quality by addressing current gaps in real-time measurement. Solutions should be accurate, rapid, scalable, and suitable for high-volume manufacturing environments.

Nomad Foods is seeking innovative in-line or on-line measurement technologies for breadcrumb-coated products (e.g., fish fingers) to enable real-time monitoring and predictive quality control. Current production processes lack sufficient measurement of critical attributes during manufacturing, making it challenging to ensure consistent product quality. Key Technical Requirements: - Ability to measure particle size distribution across individual products and batches - Capture surface area and topography of coated products - Assess breadcrumb particle porosity and internal structure - Enable predictive modelling of sensory-related texture attributes (e.g., crispiness, oiliness, hardness) based on measurement data - Operate in high-speed, high-volume environments with minimal disruption to existing lines - Deliver accurate, rapid, and scalable solutions suitable for frozen food manufacturing Evaluation Criteria Proposals will be assessed based on: - Technical Feasibility – Accuracy, reliability, and ability to measure specified attributes in real-time - Integration Capability – Ease of implementation within existing production lines - Scalability – Suitability for high-volume manufacturing environments - Predictive Capability – Ability to link measurements to sensory outcomes - Cost and ROI – Competitive cost structure and clear value proposition - Innovation Level – Novelty and potential to deliver step-change improvements in quality control Possible solution areas - Imaging systems (e.g., 2D/3D vision, hyperspectral imaging) - Spectroscopy or other non-destructive analytical methods - AI-driven data analytics and predictive modelling tools - Integrated solutions combining hardware and software for real-time feedback Requirements Interested in deliverable ideas although this could be at bench scale with a view to scale up and speed up.

candidate.description_text: Desired outcome: SMAR3TS project partner – Kouvola Research & Innovation Unit (LUT University) is seeking innovative approaches to build climate-resilient, regenerative regional food systems that can thrive under the intensifying pressures of climate change while advancing sustainability, nutrition and economic opportunity. Europe is confronting escalating impacts from extreme weather — from heatwaves to floods — that increasingly undermine food security, health, livelihoods and economic stability. In response, the European Commission has launched a public consultation on a new climate resilience framework aimed at making Europe stronger, safer and better prepared for future climate challenges. This framework will emphasise resilience by design, coordinated preparedness, risk reduction and innovative climate-resilient technologies across sectors. Food systems are a central component of this challenge: they are both vulnerable to climate shocks and a major driver of emissions and ecological degradation. Traditional food supply chains are optimised for cost and efficiency, not resilience or sustainability. To address this, climate-ready food systems must integrate regional value chain redesign, circular biomass utilisation, low-impact proteins, sustainable packaging and food-waste valorisation into coherent, context-specific strategies. The Kymenlaakso region — a bioeconomy, logistics and industrial hub of Finland — offers an ideal living lab for co-creating, testing and scaling regenerative food system innovations that align with emerging European prioriites and strategic agenda of shaping climate resilience actions. Within SMAR3TS, this I3X aims to accelerate food systems' approaches that contribute to climate resilience at the regional and EU levels.

Desired outcome: We’re supporting an established developer and manufacturer of consumer health and personal care products exploring how hair analysis solutions could be used to assess systemic health (from consumer wellness to medical conditions), measuring everything from hormones and metabolites to proteins and inorganic elements. Solutions with the potential for use at home are of particular interest. We’re keen to hear from organisations working on solutions to measure relevant biomarkers, precursors and chemical elements from the hair shaft (not the hair follicle) linked to disease states, particularly those at proof-of-concept (or later) relating to : - portable or miniaturised analytical platforms for home use - lab-on-a-chip, immunoassay or laboratory based services with the potential for consumer use (in person or by a service)

The client and market Our client is an established developer and manufacturer of consumer health and personal care products based on robust scientific principles. The market has seen an increase in consumers proactively managing and monitoring their health and wellness , investing in devices for use inside the home in addition to subscriptions and advice via 3rd parties. The provision of personalised metrics and insights that can be used to influence and improve the health of consumers is a growing space and the client is continually evaluating ways to leverage and build on their current product portfolio. The search The use of hair as a sample to investigate environmental exposure (e.g. to chemicals, toxins or drugs) has historically found applications in forensic science, medicine and environmental studies. It is often preferred over blood, urine, stool or tissue samples because it is easy to collect and handle and can provide a chronological and retrospective record of exposure and physiological changes over extended periods (days to months). There is the potential for hair analysis as a prognostic and early detection tool. The presence, within hair, of various biomarkers and specific chemicals linked to disease states may enable the identification, monitoring or prevention of conditions that may take months or years to develop (and could be missed by one-time blood or urine sampling). The client therefore wishes to identify research, techniques and service providers working on hair analysis technologies for the assessment of systemic health (from consumer wellness to medical conditions) with the ability to provide actionable insights. Opportunities could include (but are not limited to) the following examples : - Possible solution areas Discarded solutions Not DNA profiling technologies or services; Not hair analysis measuring styling related parameters. Requirements Technologies for analysis of the hair shaft (rather than hair follicle); Developed to at least proof of concept, but earlier research will be considered.

Desired outcome: As a global market leader in frozen foods, Nomad Foods is seeking to future-proof our packaging portfolio by identifying sustainable, kerbside-recyclable alternatives to our current flexible plastic bags. The solution must withstand continuous storage at -18°C and meet RecyClass RAM Grade A or B criteria, specifically optimized for the UK recycling infrastructure. We prioritize materials that can be integrated into existing manufacturing lines and are supported by case studies of successful market implementation. The ideal solution should be scalable across our global brand footprint.

None-negotiables The material must be fully compliant with food-contact regulations and demonstrate zero migration of contaminants or odors to the product. The solution must maintain its structural integrity and barrier properties under continuous frozen storage at -18°C. The packaging must be robust enough to withstand a weight of up to 2kg without tearing, stretching, or losing seal integrity. The material should offer a "Premium Feel" Must achieve a Grade A rating based on the RecyClass Recyclability Assessment Method (RAM) and be compatible with UK kerbside recycling infrastructure. Nice to have Strong interest in moving away from traditional polymers toward renewable sources. Open to exploring high-performance paper-based or bio-based polymers that do not compromise the protective barrier. Preference for transparent substrates that allow consumers to see the product While currently focused on microwave/frozen usage, the ability to withstand extreme temperatures in Air Fryers and Conventional Ovens is a significant advantage. Technical requirements The material must possess low thermal conductivity to ensure it remains safe for manual handling immediately upon removal from either freezer or a cooking appliance The packaging must feature an intuitive structure that allows consumers to easily identify and operate the opening mechanism or "tear point", reducing dependency on printed instructions. The solution must be fully food-contact safe, guaranteeing that no migration occurs that could adversely affect the quality, texture, taste, or aroma of the food throughout its entire shelf life. Discarded solutions -We are excluding any complex, multi-material plastic films (such as traditional PE/PET or PE/BOPP structures) that are not currently compatible with standard UK kerbside recycling streams or fail to meet the RecyClass Grade A/B criteria -Solutions that require specialized industrial composting facilities or fail to degrade within standard household recycling chains are not under consideration, as the disposal process must be simple and intuitive for the end consumer. Possible solution areas Bio-based polymers - Wood, Paper, Plastic lined paper, Seaweed, Plants

candidate.description_text:
Desired outcome: As a global market leader in the frozen food sector, Nomad Foods is seeking advanced material solutions capable of maintaining structural and chemical integrity across an extreme thermal lifecycle: from deep-freeze storage at -18°C to active cooking in microwaves, air fryers, and conventional ovens (up to 220°C). The material must not adversely affect the product in any way: Proposals must demonstrate that the material has zero organoleptic impact, ensuring no migration of taste, odor, or aroma to the food product throughout its lifecycle. To ensure the long-term sustainability of our packaging portfolio, the material must achieve a RecyClass Recyclability Assessment Method (RAM) rating of Grade A or B. This may be accomplished through the use of an appropriate barrier coating or by utilising an existing recyclable substrate. The packaging format remains open, though our preference is to identify solutions that could replace our current flexible plastic cook‑in pouches or trays. The technology we are seeking should be at the functional prototype stage. The proposed packaging format must enable a high-performance "cook-in-pack" solution for our consumers. This technology will facilitate steam-cooking directly within the bag, pouch, or enclosed material, preserving the nutritional integrity of the food. The material must offer high transparency, allowing consumers to see the product, allowing us to showcase our vibrant, high-quality ingredients, emphasizing the premium nature and freshness of the Nomad Foods portfolio.

Non-negotiables - The material must be food-contact safe and strictly non-migratory; it must not contaminate or alter the sensory profile of the product under high-heat stress. - Full compatibility with frozen chain logistics and home storage at a constant -18°C. - Strong structure which would not bend or weaken throughout freezing or cooking process. - Must achieve a RecyClass RAM Grade A or B Nice to have - Preference for plastic-free solutions, open to explore paper-based, or high-performance bio-based polymers that do not compromise the moisture barrier. - Transparency that allows consumers to view the product. We are open to collaborating on the development of a joint patent where appropriate, ensuring the solution can be tailored specifically to our requirements. However, any such collaboration must not restrict or limit our ability to fully utilise the packaging across our operations. Any resulting intellectual property arrangements must therefore preserve our freedom to operate and apply the packaging as needed within our business. Technical Requirements The solution should remain thermally stable enough for safe manual removal from a 220°C cooking appliance or freezer at -18°C, without collapsing or deforming. The solution must be completely inert and have no impact on the food’s quality, texture, taste, or aroma, preserving Nomad Foods’ premium standards throughout the entire lifecycle. Potential solutions will undergo a rigorous 24-month storage test at -18°C. This period includes regular quality reviews and sensory evaluations to ensure zero degradation of both the material and the food. The material must also withstand high-heat stress in home appliances (microwaves, air fryers, and ovens), reaching temperatures of up to 220°C for up to 45 minutes. The technology we are seeking should be at least at a functional prototype stage. Applicants must be ready to demonstrate feasibility through shelf-life storage data and compatibility assessments with Nomad Foods’ existing high-speed manufacturing machinery. Discarded solutions Due to the specific recyclability constraints of PET within the UK market, this material is not considered a viable long-term solution for Nomad Foods. We are not interested in bio-based polymers that cannot be processed through standard, existing recycling infrastructure. We discard any solution that complicates the end-consumer experience; materials that will not be compatible with standard household recycling chains should be dismissed. As were looking to future proof of packaging in alignment with PPWR, if the solution is not classified as Amber or Green RAM rating, then this should be dismissed. Bio-based polymers - Wood, Paper, Plastic lined paper, Seaweed, Plants

Potential solutions will undergo a rigorous 24-month storage test at -18°C. This period includes regular quality reviews and sensory evaluations to ensure zero degradation of both the material and the food. The material must also withstand high-heat stress in home appliances (microwaves, air fryers, and ovens), reaching temperatures of up to 220°C for up to 45 minutes. The technology we are seeking should be at least at a functional prototype stage. Applicants must be ready to demonstrate feasibility through shelf-life storage data and compatibility assessments with Nomad Foods’ existing high-speed manufacturing machinery. Discarded solutions Due to the specific recyclability constraints of PET within the UK market, this material is not considered a viable long-term solution for Nomad Foods. We are not interested in bio-based polymers that cannot be processed through standard, existing recycling infrastructure. We discard any solution that complicates the end-consumer experience; materials that will not be compatible with standard household recycling chains should be dismissed. As were looking to future proof of packaging in alignment with PPWR, if the solution is not classified as Amber or Green RAM rating, then this should be dismissed. Bio-based polymers - Wood, Paper, Plastic lined paper, Seaweed, Plants

Desired outcome: Traditional consumer testing methods are simply too slow, too expensive, and create high cost-per-concept friction. To maintain our relentless pace of market disruption, we are seeking a visionary technology collaborator to help us deploy an all-in-one, automated, AI-driven Agile Innovation Engine. We want to completely compress traditional learning cycles from weeks or months down to mere hours or days. If your platform can seamlessly merge high-throughput automated quantitative screening with real-time, AI-moderated qualitative focus groups, you can help us redefine how the world's favorite foods go from concept to shelf.We are seeking an enterprise-grade market research platform to upgrade our traditional innovation system into an Agile Innovation Engine. The ideal solution must replace slow, high cost-per-concept testing loops with an automated pipeline capable of rapid screening and high-volume concept analysis. We require submission proposals from technology providers offering advanced AI capabilities that can cleanly ingest early concepts, track real-time qualitative nuance, and establish reliable standardized KPIs to support compressed go/kill/refine decision cycles.

The proposed system must resolve the traditional concept testing bottlenecks and align seamlessly across two core structural tracks : The Concept Engine (Screening & Prioritization): Must support automated, high-throughput quantitative screening . It must utilize instant monadic polling to isolate individual ideas and MaxDiff testing to force-rank distinct features. The Validation Engine (Refining the Experience): Must bridge quantitative metrics with qualitative feedback using real-time insights . Data Hub and Benchmarking: Must possess an isolated, encrypted, and protected enterprise insights database that continually aggregates learning to form reusable benchmark norms for predictive categorization over time. NICE TO HAVE: Needs to incorporate AI-powered moderation to execute virtual focus groups and one-on-one virtual consumer interviews seamlessly . Targeted Optimization Capability: Platforms must facilitate comprehensive sensory alignment including flavor profiles validation , packaging heatmapping , production-to-willingness price testing , and structured logs for in-home usability experiences . DISCARDED SOLUTIONS: ​ Traditional, facility-based brick-and-mortar focus groups due to extensive operational and logistical timelines . Sequential testing models that isolate quantitative data from qualitative context, creating delayed learning windows spanning weeks or months . Siloed, single-vendor analytical testing tools that require fragmented hand-offs and lack cross-category or cross-market data normalization . Partnering with us offers an unprecedented runway for growth: Massive Global Scale: Gain immediate validation for your technology by embedding it into the core R&D pipeline of a global industry titan. Substantial Commercial Pilot Funding: Backed by an earmarked project budget, this initiative isn’t a theoretical exercise—it is a fast-tracked, heavily resourced path to a live corporate integration . True Innovation Autonomy: We are moving away from restrictive, legacy methodologies . We want your cutting-edge tools to dictate our future workflows, giving your platform the center stage to showcase its full capabilities. Long-Term Strategic Alliance: A successful pilot will position your company as our primary infrastructure partner for enterprise-wide product testing, unlocking recurring global revenue streams.

candidate.description_text:
Desired outcome: Nomad Foods is seeking innovative equipment, processing technologies, or integrated solutions that enable the development of next-generation tempura batter-coated fish products. By “conventional” battering and coating systems, we mean standard waterfall/curtain batter application combined with static frying or baking, which limits coating uniformity, consistency, and yield at scale. We are looking for solutions that demonstrably improve on this baseline by delivering: a more even and well-adhered batter coating across irregular fish portions, reduced batter loss/waste during application, and greater batch-to-batch consistency of coating weight and texture. We expect proposals exclusively from commercial technology providers — equipment manufacturers, engineering firms, technology start-ups, and system integrators with deployable or near-deployable solutions. Academic institutions or research groups without a commercial product, prototype, or industrial partner are not the focus of this call. By “improve robustness” we mean equipment and processes that maintain consistent coating performance despite normal variability in raw material (fish portion size and shape), batter viscosity, and line speed, with minimal downtime or operator intervention. By “flexibility for integration” we mean compatibility with our existing battering/coating and freezing lines: solutions that can be retrofitted or integrated without requiring a full line replacement, and that can accommodate multiple product formats (fillets, portions, nuggets) on the same equipment.

Nomad Foods aims to explore advanced battering and coating technologies that move beyond conventional systems and enable future tempura product platforms. Solutions may involve novel application methods, equipment design, process control, or system integration that improve robustness, efficiency, and product performance across frozen fish supply chains. Proposals will be evaluated based on: • Ability to demonstrably enable next-generation tempura batter-coated fish products • Industrial scalability and compatibility with frozen fish manufacturing • Technology readiness level and maturity, and a credible path to industrial deployment • Supplier track record and relevant industrial references • Flexibility for integration within our existing manufacturing environments Both ready-to-deploy solutions and technologies requiring limited co-development will be considered. Expected Technology Readiness Level (TRL): We are looking for ready to makert technology but also we are also open to both early-stage lab/pilot-scale proof of concept (TRL 3–4) and factory-ready, proven solutions (TRL 7+). Please state the current TRL of your proposed solution and the expected path to industrial deployment. Geographic Scope: We welcome proposals from providers and solutions based in any region globally. Proposed solutions must comply with the food safety regulations applicable at the site of deployment, and the provider must be able to support installation, commissioning, and after-sales service at the relevant Nomad Foods manufacturing site (location to be confirmed during discussions). Technical requirements Must-have: • Suitable for frozen fish/seafood manufacturing environments • Food-grade, hygienic design compliant with applicable food safety regulations at the deployment site • Industrially scalable (pilot to full-scale factory application) • Compatible with high-throughput, continuous processing lines • Capable of maintaining batter temperature within during application Nice-to-have: • Able to operate across a range of tempura batter viscosities and formats • Modular or retrofittable design compatible with existing line footprint • Real-time process monitoring or automated coating-weight control • Reduced batter consumption/waste versus conventional waterfall application Operational ranges: • Batter temperature during application: 4–8°C • Product format/size range to be coated: 20-250g per piece Discarded solutions Standard waterfall/curtain tempura batter applicators — already trialled and do not meet our consistency and waste-reduction requirements. Possible solution areas We encourage submissions leveraging technologies such as electrostatic batter application, ultrasonic spray coating, rotary drum or curtain coating with adaptive control, vacuum-assisted batter pick-up, or other novel application and process-control methods relevant to tempura-style coatings. We are particularly interested in hearing from equipment manufacturers, process engineering firms, and technology integrators with experience in food or seafood coating lines.

Desired outcome: Lacer seeks substitute ingredients or formulations that deliver the same antiseptic efficacy as Chlorhexidine (CHX). The solution must reduce plaque and gingivitis with significantly fewer side effects, primarily targeting lower cytotoxicity and a strict absence of staining. We prefer an ingredient or mix of ingredients to add to existing formulations, but finished products will also be evaluated if all requirements are met. Lacer is open to Joint Development, Licensing, and Exclusivity agreements. We are actively seeking to collaborate with: Biotechnology industries and startups. Healthcare industries and companies. Ingredient suppliers. Universities and research centers Background : Chlorhexidine is a highly effective antimicrobial in oral care with a broad spectrum of action. It binds to the oral mucosa for continuous release over 5-7 hours, prolonging its effect. Despite solid clinical evidence reducing plaque and gingivitis, CHX is associated with tooth staining, taste alteration, non-selective antibacterial action, and mucosal irritation. These side effects limit consumer acceptance and generally restrict usage to a short-term 1-2 week period. The CHX market is highly commoditized and relies heavily on professional dentist recommendations. Current industry standards often use CHX at 0.12% or 0.2% combined with additional ingredients like CPC, cymenol, or allantoin to drive these recommendations. A truly differentiated alternative that delivers efficacy without side effects will drastically lower the barrier to entry and increase market share.

Must-Have Requirements Maturity: The proposed solution must be at a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of > 5. Efficacy Benchmarking: Chlorhexidine is established as the gold standard benchmark for all innovation ideas. Efficacy will be compared against CHX, utilizing public data on chlorhexidine usage as the primary reference point. In Vitro Proof: Solutions must demonstrate in vitro efficacy using multispecies biofilm models. Mandatory Non-Staining: The absence of staining is a mandatory requirement; submissions must include in vitro data proving minimal to no tooth staining. Sensorial Profile: The formulation must possess acceptable sensorial and organoleptic characteristics. Specifically, the solution must strictly avoid any bitterness or metallic taste. Format Stability: The technology must maintain good stability and solubility in a liquid format, such as a mouthwash. Viability: Solutions must be scalable, cost-effective, and possess a positive consumer safety profile. Geographical & Regulatory Scope: The regulatory and commercial focus includes the European Union, Spain, and Latin America. Ingredients must meet cosmetic legislation, specifically requiring AEMPS approval for personal care products in Spain. Nice-to-Haves Selective Microbiology: Alternatives should ideally possess a selective microbiology profile, supported by clear microbiome studies. Complementary Innovations: The challenge is inclusive of potential tools from other industries, such as cosmetic tools, that could complement current products. Less cytotoxicity Less irritation (with the aim of enabling long-term use) Possible solution areas Ingredient industries | Biotechnology | Healthcare | Medical devices | Antimicrobial | Chlorhexidine alternative | Oral Care | Mouthwash Formulation

Desired outcome: A leading company in the dental industry is seeking to identify and validate novel, intrinsically safer teeth whitening technologies to launch a best-in-class whitening kit for both pharmacy and e-commerce channels. The successful solution must feature low or non-oxygen/peroxide release to minimize free radical exposure, operate at a safe, enamel-friendly pH (> 5.5), and guarantee a strict shelf-life stability of at least 30 months without compromising efficacy. We are open to various business relationships, with a strong preference for: - Finished product supply / Private label manufacturing - Joint Development (specifically for highly promising T4-T5 technologies) - Licensing and Exclusivity agreements Background While many current teeth whitening products deliver rapid results, they often rely heavily on peroxide-driven oxygen release. These mechanisms generate free radicals that can cause enamel damage and hypersensitivity. Alternatively, some products utilize highly acidic formulations (pH < 5.5) that require complex protective measures for the consumer. Our goal is to overcome this industry compromise. We are looking for breakthrough formulations or active ingredients that deliver clinical efficacy comparable to current market leaders, but utilizing significantly safer, low-oxygen, or peroxide-free mechanisms.

Must-Have Requirements Safety First (Low Free Radicals): The technology must be non-hydrogen peroxide-based or utilize significantly lower levels of peroxide to strictly minimize free radical generation and oxygen usage. Critical Stability & Shelf-Life: The formulation and its efficacy must remain completely stable for at least 30 months. This is a critical evaluation criterion. Submissions must prove that active ingredients and pH do not degrade over time (demonstrable via real-time or accelerated 6-month testing). pH Requirements: The formulation must maintain a strict, stable pH > 5.5 to ensure enamel safety. Efficacy Benchmarking: Submissions must demonstrate proven whitening efficacy in vitro and in vivo (targeting an improvement of roughly 9 tones within 7 days). Slightly lower efficacy (e.g., 1 tone less or requiring up to 12 days) is acceptable only if the technology offers zero oxygen release. PAP Specifications: If the formula utilizes PAP (Phthalimidoperoxycaproic acid), it must be present at a minimum concentration of 2%. Regulatory Compliance: The solution must fully comply with EU cosmetic regulatory requirements for convenient at-home consumer use. Maturity: The proposed solution must be at a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of > 5. Geographical Scope: Solutions must be commercially viable within Spain. Nice-to-have Adjunct Synergies: The inclusion of adjunct technologies or devices (like LED lights or customized trays) and synergistic ingredients (like Hydroxyapatite) is highly welcome if they demonstrably enhance safety or efficacy. Cost Feasibility: Solutions must be cost-effective and highly feasible for a premium consumer retail price point. Discarded solutions Unstable Formulations: Any formulation that fails to maintain a reliable pH > 5.5 over the required 30-month shelf life. Inconsistent Manufacturing: Solutions with limited stability data, poor batch-to-batch reproducibility, or inconsistent efficacy results. Whitening Strips: Due to historically low efficacy and poor consumer acceptance in our target market, strip formats are entirely out of scope. Possible solution areas Teeth Whitening | Oral Care | Non-Peroxide | Low Oxygen Release | Free Radical Safety | PAP | Dental Aesthetics | Cosmetic Dentistry | Private Label Manufacturing

These mechanisms generate free radicals that can cause enamel damage and hypersensitivity. Alternatively, some products utilize highly acidic formulations (pH < 5.5) that require complex protective measures for the consumer. Our goal is to overcome this industry compromise. We are looking for breakthrough formulations or active ingredients that deliver clinical efficacy comparable to current market leaders, but utilizing significantly safer, low-oxygen, or peroxide-free mechanisms.

Must-Have Requirements Safety First (Low Free Radicals): The technology must be non-hydrogen peroxide-based or utilize significantly lower levels of peroxide to strictly minimize free radical generation and oxygen usage. Critical Stability & Shelf-Life: The formulation and its efficacy must remain completely stable for at least 30 months. This is a critical evaluation criterion. Submissions must prove that active ingredients and pH do not degrade over time (demonstrable via real-time or accelerated 6-month testing). pH Requirements: The formulation must maintain a strict, stable pH > 5.5 to ensure enamel safety. Efficacy Benchmarking: Submissions must demonstrate proven whitening efficacy in vitro and in vivo (targeting an improvement of roughly 9 tones within 7 days). Slightly lower efficacy (e.g., 1 tone less or requiring up to 12 days) is acceptable only if the technology offers zero oxygen release. PAP Specifications: If the formula utilizes PAP (Phthalimidoperoxycaproic acid), it must be present at a minimum concentration of 2%. Regulatory Compliance: The solution must fully comply with EU cosmetic regulatory requirements for convenient at-home consumer use. Maturity: The proposed solution must be at a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of > 5. Geographical Scope: Solutions must be commercially viable within Spain. Nice-to-have Adjunct Synergies: The inclusion of adjunct technologies or devices (like LED lights or customized trays) and synergistic ingredients (like Hydroxyapatite) is highly welcome if they demonstrably enhance safety or efficacy. Cost Feasibility: Solutions must be cost-effective and highly feasible for a premium consumer retail price point. Discarded solutions Unstable Formulations: Any formulation that fails to maintain a reliable pH > 5.5 over the required 30-month shelf life. Inconsistent Manufacturing: Solutions with limited stability data, poor batch-to-batch reproducibility, or inconsistent efficacy results. Whitening Strips: Due to historically low efficacy and poor consumer acceptance in our target market, strip formats are entirely out of scope. Possible solution areas Teeth Whitening | Oral Care | Non-Peroxide | Low Oxygen Release | Free Radical Safety | PAP | Dental Aesthetics | Cosmetic Dentistry | Private Label Manufacturing

candidate.description_text:
Desired outcome: We are looking for a material /process that allows to inject a flexible sealing / fluid barrier in particular areas of an already assembled device and that can fill gaps in the range of 1 mm – 3 mm between movable and fixed parts.

Personal care devices are often used under wet conditions. In order to ensure a delightful use experience over time the entry of fluids in various parts of the device must be prevented. Particular in areas with moving parts and small gaps and overall limited space traditional (rubber based), assembled sealings are difficult to implement. Requirements The sealing need to allow the movable part a motion of up to ± 1mm at a frequency of up to 160 Hz, with minimum dampening to the system. The sealing must be durable for an operation time of at least 12 h. The sealing material must be safe for close human use, which can be ensured by food grade, medical grade or FDA-compliant materials. Furthermore, the material should be resistant against typical personal care products that are used in combination with the person care devices. Possible solution areas Possible solutions areas can include, but are not limited to, self expanding, high flexible foam or silicone gel adhesives. Already commercially available solutions which need minimal additional development effort are highly appreciated. Discarded solutions Materials without potential of release for human use or just ideas in fundament research state.

L’obiettivo è sviluppare e validare una piattaforma di assistenza basata su intelligenza artificiale, affidabile e conforme alle normative, per supportare decisioni tecniche e operative in agricoltura e silvicoltura. candidate.description_text: Abstract Un istituto di ricerca tedesco specializzato in tecnologie di produzione cerca partner europei per un progetto di ricerca finanziato dall’UE. Il consorzio ideale include first responder, autorità pubbliche, sviluppatori di droni e sensori e amministrazioni locali. Budget atteso ~4 M€ e target TRL 7-8.
